turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr. Iyer, please come through. I will note your observations before Doctor Menon sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you madam. I am a bit late, traffic from Whitefield was completely stuck.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): With this rain the Outer Ring Road is always like that. Did you get wet?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a little. I was telling my wife, this weather is better for sitting at home and watching cricket.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): You watched the India match last night?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Full match. That last over I was standing in the hall. My grandson was on the phone from Pune, he is eight, he knows every player's name.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Eight years and already a commentator. Who does he like?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Kohli only. Poster above the bed. We were arguing about the pitch, he says it was turning, I said it was just the dew in the second innings.
[SEG0009] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Dew changes the whole game, no?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Exactly. And my wife made filter coffee in the middle, we finished the dabba of mixture. He wants an English willow bat for his birthday, I told him ask your father.
[SEG0011] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Birthdays get expensive. Alright, sleeve up, sit still for the blood pressure.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): One second. He also copied the celebration, the helmet one, in our living room. The lamp almost went.
[SEG0013] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sounds lively. Please don't talk for a moment while the cuff finishes.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry sorry. I will keep quiet.
[SEG0015] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-six. Pulse is eighty-eight. Oxygen saturation ninety-five percent. Breathing rate is eighteen per minute.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety-five, is that alright? I feel short of breath on the stairs at home.

[SEG0017] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor will discuss that with you. I also have this morning's spirometry. FEV1 is one point eight litres, that is sixty-two percent predicted, and the FEV1 to FVC ratio is zero point six four.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't follow those figures madam. Just tell me if it is serious.
[SEG0019] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Not for me to say. On your prescription slip, Foracort two hundred micrograms is written as two puffs twice a day.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Two puffs? No. The chest doctor said one puff in the morning and one at night. I am sure. Two hundred itself feels strong.
[SEG0021] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can only read what is printed, two puffs twice daily. Please sort the dose with Doctor Menon. He is free now.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Printed things are sometimes wrong only. I have been doing one puff, and that also when I remember.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr. Iyer, good morning. I am Doctor Menon. Priya has given me the numbers. What brought you in today?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning doctor. Mainly this cough. Every morning I am coughing, and the breathlessness is also there.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has the morning cough been going on?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): That I cannot say exactly. Maybe from last monsoon. Or even before, I don't remember the month.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will leave the start date open for now. Is the cough dry, or is there phlegm?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Phlegm is there in the morning, white, sometimes a little yellow. Not the whole day. After I wash my face it settles somewhat.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the phlegm?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Blood? No no, nothing like that. I would have come running.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the breathlessness, when do you notice it?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): When I climb to the second floor, or if I walk fast to the bus stop. On flat ground, if I go slow, it is okay. At night I am not gasping.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with it?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Wait, before that, the yellow colour, my wife said it was more during the infection. Now it is mostly white.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will come to the infection. Chest pain, yes or no?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. No tightness also. Just the air not coming fully.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever in the last few days?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Not now. During the chest infection I had fever, that has gone.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell me about that infection.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): About three weeks back. Cough became much more, fever for four days, the local doctor said chest infection. He gave me azithromycin.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): What dose of azithromycin, and did you finish it?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Five hundred milligrams, once a day, five days. I finished the strip last week. I am not taking it now.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Any wheeze, a whistling sound, when you breathe out?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes in the morning, yes, a small whistle. It goes after the blue pump, if I use it.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): The blue pump is Asthalin, salbutamol?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Asthalin, yes, hundred microgram, two puffs when I need. But I don't use it properly, some days I skip, maybe once in two three days only.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): So it is prescribed two puffs as needed, but you are not taking it that way. And the Foracort?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Foracort also on and off. Priya said the paper shows two puffs, I still think it is one. I cannot be sure I take it every day.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will not lock the Foracort dose today until we see the original strip. Do you smoke?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Little bit only. About ten a day.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ten cigarettes?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, maybe twenty. Some days more if there is tension in the office. I should not minimise, you doctors always catch it.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many years has that been?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Since I joined the bank. That is, um, thirty years? Thirty-two? Something like that. Long time.
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still working at the bank?
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Retired last year. Now I am at home, apart from the society committee. Too many meetings, too much tea.
[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other regular medicines? Blood pressure tablets, sugar tablets?
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Sugar is normal, they checked in January. For pressure I take amlodipine, five milligrams, morning, since four years. That one I don't miss.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anyone discussed your lungs before, a name like COPD or asthma?
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): The local doctor said chronic bronchitis, not asthma. He said my lungs are tired from the smoking. I don't know the English term they use now.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am going to listen to your chest. Deep breath in, please. And out.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Like this? My grandson says I breathe like our old ceiling fan, noisy.

[SEG0063] person_3 (DOCTOR): There is a wheeze on both sides, a bit more on the right. Air entry is reduced at the bases. No crackles today. Heart sounds are normal, no swelling of the ankles that I can see.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): The right side was paining during the infection, not now. Sorry, you said no pain, I already told no.

[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me summarise. Morning cough with some white phlegm for an uncertain time, breathlessness on climbing and fast walking, a chest infection about three weeks ago that settled after azithromycin, and you still smoke, somewhere between ten and twenty cigarettes a day. Inhalers are irregular. Does that match?
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly yes. The phlegm was yellower before, now white. And I am not breathless sitting here talking to you.

[SEG0067] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sitting at rest you are comfortable, noted. My working impression is chronic obstructive lung disease, likely COPD, with a recent infective flare that has settled. I cannot fully separate chronic bronchitis from that, but I am not calling it asthma.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): COPD. That is the word. Is it reversible if I stop smoking?

[SEG0069] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stopping will not rewind everything, but it is the most useful step, and it slows further damage. I can refer you to our tobacco cessation counsellor, and we can start nicotine gum if you are willing.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): Gum I can try. The counsellor, if it is in this building, yes. I don't want another long trip in the rain.

[SEG0071] person_3 (DOCTOR): It is in this building, Thursday mornings. I will put the referral in. Nicotine gum, two milligrams, one piece when you crave, up to eight pieces in a day, by mouth. Start after you leave today.
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): Two milligrams, up to eight. If I feel giddy I should stop, no?

[SEG0073] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, stop and tell us if you feel giddy, vomiting, or chest pain. For the Asthalin, please use two puffs when you are breathless, not once in three days. Shake it, breathe out, then inhale slowly.
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): I will try. The Foracort, one or two?

[SEG0075] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bring the strip next time and we will fix that dose. Until then don't suddenly double it on my word alone. If the morning phlegm turns thick yellow again and you get fever, we might send a sputum test, but I am not ordering it today.
[SEG0076] person_2 (PATIENT): Understood. What about an x-ray? The local doctor talked about it and then I went out of station.
[SEG0077] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will book a chest x-ray this week, to look at the bases after that infection. Not urgent overnight.
[SEG0078] person_2 (PATIENT): This week is fine. My wife will come, she remembers the papers better than me.
[SEG0079] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please bring the Foracort strip and the old prescription. See me again in six weeks with the x-ray report, or sooner if the breathlessness suddenly worsens.
[SEG0080] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks. And if I cough blood I should not wait, I know.
[SEG0081] person_3 (DOCTOR): Correct, do not wait for six weeks if there is blood, high fever, or you cannot finish a sentence. Any questions?
[SEG0082] person_2 (PATIENT): Only, the spirometry, sixty-two percent, is that very bad?
[SEG0083] person_3 (DOCTOR): It is reduced, it fits with the COPD impression, it is not an emergency number. We will track it. Priya, he is done from my side.
[SEG0084] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I will book the x-ray and the cessation clinic on the system before you go, Mr. Iyer. Take care in the rain.
